body.statement:
Let \(\xi_n^0=(p_n/n,\gamma,\lambda,R)\), \(\widehat d_n=d(\widehat\xi_n)\), and \(I_\gamma=\mathbb E[Z^2\sigma(\gamma Z)\{1-\sigma(\gamma Z)\}]\).  On every compact set \(K\subset(0,\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}})\times(\underline\gamma,\overline\gamma)\times(0,\infty)^2\) on which the four-distance map is continuously differentiable and
\[
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\min\{d_{\mathrm{bal}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{rad}}(\xi),d_{\mathrm{col}}(\xi),d_0(\xi)\}>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty>0,
\]
uniformly in \(\xi\in K\),
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat d_n-d(\xi_n^0)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_4\!\left(0,\Omega(\xi)\right),\qquad
 \Omega(\xi)=\frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma},\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_n\to_{\mathbb P}\Omega(\xi).
\]
Consequently, the simultaneous intervals \([\widehat d_{\ell n}-\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha},\widehat d_{\ell n}+\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}]\), \(\ell\in\{\mathrm{bal},\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{col},0\}\), have joint coverage at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly on \(K\), and
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in K}\mathbb P_\xi\{\widehat s_{n,\alpha}\ne\operatorname{sgn}(\Delta_{\mathrm{HIR}}(\xi))\}\to0,
\]
where abstention counts as an error.  Thus the classifier is total, reports \(\bot\) whenever a certificate is missing or an estimated boundary distance fails to exceed \(\widehat u_{n,1-\alpha}\), and is uniformly nonabstaining and sign-consistent on compact margin-separated, derivative-nondegenerate sets.
body.justification: A deterministic diagram is operational only if its phase label can be learned from a trial away from nonregular boundaries.
body.gap: SurCandes2019 estimates scalar states for one logistic MLE and LuYangWang2025 estimates quadratic variance components; neither gives joint inference for a contrast of dependent optimized policy criteria.
body.consumer: The theorem supplies an uncertainty-aware label for whether entropy balancing improves or worsens targeting regret in a feature-expanded trial reanalysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Derivation of a locally stable, nonabstaining certified branch, its gamma derivative, and continuity of the signed HIR dividend from the original same-sample entropy weights and the globally selected nonconcave policy optimizer.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen joint-resolvent handle names overlaps and a block Jacobian but gives no state equations, no deterministic-equivalent theorem, and no global branch-selection result. Positivity of the collision-distance definition cannot establish these properties because that distance is set to zero when certification fails and the candidate branches themselves have not been constructed. The four-distance map being differentiable also does not by itself imply continuity of the signed dividend: its absolute value can be smooth while its sign changes through an unproved branch switch. Thus the scalar delta method cannot certify the stated operational classifier until the sibling joint-system target supplies branch existence, stability, and derivative consistency.
obligation.attempted: Used the established uniform likelihood limit to derive the exact one-coordinate Taylor expansion for the four-distance plug-in, covariance consistency, and the explicit rank-one Gaussian-max quantile. Then checked the abstention and sign steps separately. Margin separation controls estimated distances once a stable branch exists, but neither it nor derivative nondegeneracy constructs that branch or rules out a discontinuous signed-dividend switch. Solving those facts here would duplicate the sibling-owned joint-system target or assume its crux.
obligation.partial_result:
The scalar part and the conditional inference reduction are complete.  Let \(K\) be a compact subset of the interior parameter space, and suppose temporarily that there is an open neighborhood \(U\supset K\) on which the certified selector is nonabstaining, \(d\) is continuously differentiable, and the signed dividend
\[
 \Delta(\xi)=\lambda\{g(\rho_T(b^\star(\xi);\xi))-g(\rho_E(b^\star(\xi);\xi))\}
\]
is continuous.  Assume also that
\[
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\min_{\ell\in\{\mathrm{bal},\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{col},0\}}d_\ell(\xi)>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty>0.
\]
Because \(\widehat\xi_n-\xi_n^0=(0,\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma,0,0)^\top\), the integral form of the mean-value identity gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{d(\widehat\xi_n)-d(\xi_n^0)\}
 =\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\sqrt n(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma)+r_n,
\]
where
\[
 \|r_n\|_\infty
 \le
 \sqrt n|\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma|
 \sup_{0\le t\le1}
 \left\|\partial_\gamma d\!\left(\xi_n^0+t(\widehat\xi_n-\xi_n^0)\right)
       -\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\right\|_\infty.
\]
The already-established uniform likelihood limit implies \(\sqrt n|\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly on \(K\).  Uniform continuity of \(\partial_\gamma d\) on a compact neighborhood of \(K\), together with \(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), therefore gives \(r_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly on \(K\).  Slutsky's theorem then yields
\[
 \sqrt n\{d(\widehat\xi_n)-d(\xi_n^0)\}
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N_4\!\left(0,
 \frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \right).
\]
The consistency of \(\widehat I_{\gamma,n}\), continuity of \(\partial_\gamma d\), and the preceding consistency of \(\widehat\xi_n\) imply
\[
 \widehat\Omega_n-\frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \to_{\mathbb P}0
\]
uniformly on \(K\).  This covariance has rank one.  If \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), its Gaussian limit can be represented as \(I_\gamma^{-1/2}\partial_\gamma d(\xi)G\), and hence its simultaneous critical value is explicitly
\[
 q_{1-\alpha}\!\left(
 \frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \right)
 =z_{1-\alpha/2}\frac{\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty}{\sqrt{I_\gamma}},
\]
where \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  The derivative lower bound makes this critical value strictly positive, so plug-in consistency and the continuous mapping theorem give simultaneous coverage \(1-\alpha+o(1)\).  Finally, continuity of \(\Delta\), compactness, and \(\inf_{\xi\in K}|\Delta(\xi)|=\inf_{\xi\in K}d_0(\xi)>0\) imply uniform local constancy of its sign.  All four estimated distances remain above their vanishing critical radius with probability tending to one, and the conditional classifier is therefore uniformly nonabstaining and sign-consistent.

What is not supplied by the frozen core is the temporary neighborhood premise: the joint same-sample entropy-tilt and nonconcave policy problem has not been reduced to explicit state equations, so nonabstention, local branch stability, differentiability of \(d\), and continuity of the signed \(\Delta\) cannot yet be derived.  These are precisely the outputs owned by the unresolved joint-system target and cannot be promoted to assumptions here.
